## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for collecting stormwater runoff samples
from urban and peri-urban watersheds during wet-weather events. Storm
runoff is a primary pathway by which sediments, nutrients, metals,
bacteria, and other pollutants enter receiving waters. Characterizing
stormwater quality is essential for assessing nonpoint source pollution,
evaluating the effectiveness of best management practices (BMPs), and
supporting compliance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination
System (NPDES) Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) permit
requirements.

The procedures described here are consistent with the California State
Water Resources Control Board's Surface Water Ambient Monitoring
Program (SWAMP) guidance and the State Water Board's Stormwater
Sampling Guidance Document for construction and industrial general
permits.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Manual grab and time-composite sampling of stormwater
  runoff from outfalls, storm drains, open channels, sheet flow, and
  receiving streams during and immediately following precipitation
  events
- **Does not apply to:** Dry-weather urban runoff (use
  [SOP-F41 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F41-surface-water-sampling.qmd));
  automated composite sampling with programmed autosamplers (requires a
  separate instrument-specific SOP); industrial facility compliance
  sampling governed by site-specific Stormwater Pollution Prevention
  Plans (SWPPPs)
- **Location:** All EA Program stormwater monitoring sites in the
  greater Los Angeles basin and Inland Empire watersheds


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve sampling plan and storm-event criteria          |
| Field Lead        | Monitor weather forecasts, mobilize crew, verify equipment |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and handle samples per this SOP                 |
| New Students      | Complete training before participating in storm sampling |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Drowning and flash flooding:** Stormwater channels and storm drains
  can fill rapidly during precipitation. Water levels can rise without
  warning. Never enter a storm drain, culvert, or engineered channel
  during active flow.
- **Slippery surfaces:** Wet concrete, asphalt, and channel banks are
  extremely slippery. Wear non-slip footwear.
- **Traffic:** Many outfalls are located near roadways. Wear high-
  visibility clothing and use traffic cones.
- **Electrical:** Lightning is a hazard during thunderstorms. Suspend
  sampling and seek shelter if lightning is observed or thunder is
  heard.
- **Biological/Chemical:** Urban runoff may contain pathogens, trash,
  petroleum products, and other contaminants. Avoid skin contact and
  ingestion.
- **Reduced visibility:** Storm sampling frequently occurs at night or
  in low-visibility conditions. Carry headlamps and flashlights.
:::

### 4.1 Required PPE

- [ ] Waterproof rain gear (jacket and pants)
- [ ] Non-slip waterproof boots or wading boots
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (double-glove recommended)
- [ ] High-visibility vest or jacket
- [ ] Headlamp and backup flashlight
- [ ] Personal flotation device (PFD) if sampling near deep or swift
      channels

### 4.2 Safety Rules

- **Never sample alone.** A minimum of two people must be present.
- **Never enter a storm drain or culvert** during active flow.
- **Never wade into a channel** if water is above knee height or
  velocity makes footing uncertain.
- **Establish an escape route** before approaching any sampling
  location.
- **Monitor upstream conditions.** If water is rising, retreat
  immediately.
- If lightning is observed, cease sampling and move to a vehicle or
  enclosed structure. Wait 30 minutes after the last observed
  lightning before resuming.

### 4.3 Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for
general emergency response. If a team member is swept into a channel,
call 911 immediately. Do not attempt an in-water rescue unless you
have swift-water rescue training and equipment.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Pre-labeled sample bottles            | Provided by analytical lab; type and preservative per analyte (see Section 8) |
| Polypropylene grab-sample bottles (1 L) | For general chemistry and nutrients    |
| Sterile 100 mL Colilert bottles       | With sodium thiosulfate for bacteria; see [SOP-L49](../lab_sops/SOP-L49-colilert-quanti-tray.qmd) |
| Extension pole with bottle clamp      | For sampling from bridges, banks, or above outfalls |
| Stainless steel or HDPE bucket        | For flow-weighted composites             |
| Graduated cylinder or measuring cup   | For volumetric aliquots into composites  |
| Deionized water                       | For equipment blanks and rinsing         |
| Syringe and 0.45 um filters           | For dissolved analyte samples            |

### Field Documentation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Field data sheets (waterproof paper)  | Record time, sample ID, conditions       |
| Chain of custody (COC) forms          | Required for lab submission              |
| Camera (waterproof)                   | Photo-document site conditions           |
| Rain gauge (manual or tipping bucket) | For recording on-site precipitation      |

### Transport and Storage

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Coolers with ice                      | Maintain samples at 4 C during transport |
| Custody seals                         | For sealing coolers before shipment      |
| Ziploc bags                           | For protecting field sheets and labels   |


## 6. Storm Event Criteria

### 6.1 Qualifying Storm Events

A qualifying storm event for stormwater sampling must meet all of the
following criteria unless the project sampling plan specifies
otherwise:

- **Antecedent dry period:** At least 72 hours (3 days) of dry weather
  (no measurable precipitation) preceding the storm
- **Minimum rainfall:** At least 2.5 mm (0.1 inches) of total
  precipitation predicted or observed
- **Duration:** Sufficient to produce runoff at the sampling location

### 6.2 Storm Tracking and Mobilization

1. Begin monitoring weather forecasts 3--5 days in advance using the
   National Weather Service (weather.gov) and local radar
2. When a qualifying event is forecast, alert the sampling crew and
   confirm availability
3. Pre-stage equipment and coolers at least 12 hours before the
   predicted onset of rain
4. Deploy to sampling locations when precipitation begins or when
   runoff is observed at the outfall
5. Record the date and time that rainfall began (from weather station
   data or field observation)


## 7. Procedure

### 7.1 First-Flush Grab Sampling

The first flush is the initial period of stormwater discharge, which
typically carries the highest pollutant concentrations. For most
NPDES and research applications, first-flush samples should be
collected within the first one to two hours of discharge.

1. Arrive at the sampling location before or shortly after the onset
   of runoff
2. Record the time, weather conditions (rainfall intensity, wind,
   temperature), and visual observations (color, turbidity, odor,
   floating debris, oil sheen) on the field data sheet
3. Put on clean nitrile gloves. Do not touch your face, hair, or any
   non-sampling surfaces.
4. If sampling from an outfall pipe or channel bank, attach the sample
   bottle to the extension pole
5. Collect the grab sample by submerging the bottle directly in the
   flowing runoff, mouth facing upstream (or into the flow), at
   approximately mid-depth. Avoid disturbing sediment at the bottom.
6. Fill the bottle to the appropriate level for the analyte. Leave
   headspace for samples that require mixing but not for volatile
   analytes.
7. Cap immediately. Wipe the exterior with a clean paper towel.
8. Label the bottle with: site ID, date, time, sample type (grab),
   sampler initials
9. Place immediately in a cooler with ice
10. If bacteria samples are being collected, collect them first to
    minimize holding time. Fill sterile Colilert bottles to the 100 mL
    line per [SOP-L49](../lab_sops/SOP-L49-colilert-quanti-tray.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
### First-Flush Timing

To qualify as a first-flush sample under most California general
permits, the sample must be collected during the first two hours of
discharge from a storm event that follows at least 72 hours of dry
weather.
:::

### 7.2 Time-Composite Sampling (Manual)

Time-composite samples characterize the event-mean concentration
(EMC) of pollutants over the duration of a storm. Composites are
assembled from individual grab aliquots collected at regular time
intervals.

1. Determine the composite interval based on the expected storm
   duration. For a 4-hour storm, collect aliquots every 15--30
   minutes.
2. At each interval, collect a 200--500 mL grab aliquot using a
   clean polypropylene bottle or HDPE bucket
3. Measure and record the volume of each aliquot
4. Pour each aliquot into a single, pre-cleaned composite container
   (typically a 4 L HDPE bottle). Keep the composite container on ice
   between aliquots.
5. After the final aliquot, mix the composite thoroughly and
   distribute into the appropriate sample bottles for each analyte
6. Preserve, label, and store as described in Section 8

### 7.3 Flow-Weighted Composite Sampling (Manual)

Flow-weighted composites provide a more accurate estimate of EMC than
time composites because the volume of each aliquot is proportional to
the flow rate at the time of collection.

1. Estimate or measure discharge at each sampling interval using a
   bucket-and-stopwatch method, staff gauge, or flow meter
2. Calculate the aliquot volume for each interval as:

$$
V_i = V_{\text{total}} \times \frac{Q_i}{\sum Q_i}
$$

where $V_i$ is the aliquot volume, $Q_i$ is the flow rate at
interval $i$, and $V_{\text{total}}$ is the target composite volume

3. Collect and combine aliquots into the composite container as in
   Section 7.2
4. Record flow estimates and aliquot volumes on the field data sheet

### 7.4 Sheet-Flow Sampling

For diffuse overland flow (e.g., from parking lots, lawns, or
agricultural fields) where no defined outfall exists:

1. Identify a low point or convergence zone where sheet flow
   concentrates
2. Place a clean stainless steel or HDPE tray or shallow pan at ground
   level to intercept the flow
3. Transfer collected water to sample bottles using a clean syringe or
   by pouring directly
4. Record the contributing area and surface type (impervious,
   pervious, mixed)


## 8. Sample Preservation and Holding Times

Follow [SOP-F41 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F41-surface-water-sampling.qmd)
Section 9 for general preservation and handling procedures. The table
below lists common stormwater analytes:

| Analyte              | Container          | Preservative           | Holding Time    |
|:---------------------|:-------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------|
| pH                   | Poly, 250 mL       | None; analyze in field | 15 minutes      |
| Conductivity         | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 C        | 28 days         |
| TSS / SSC            | Poly, 1 L          | Refrigerate 4 C        | 7 days          |
| Turbidity            | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 C        | 48 hours        |
| Nitrate + nitrite    | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Ammonia              | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Total phosphorus     | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Ortho-phosphate      | Poly, 250 mL       | Filter 0.45 um; 4 C   | 48 hours        |
| Total metals         | Poly, 500 mL       | HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 6 months        |
| Dissolved metals     | Poly, 500 mL       | Filter 0.45 um; HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 6 months |
| Total coliforms / *E. coli* | Sterile, 100 mL | Na~2~S~2~O~3~ (if chlorinated); 4 C | 6 hours |
| Oil and grease       | Glass, 1 L         | HCl to pH < 2; 4 C    | 28 days         |

::: {.callout-note}
Confirm specific container types, preservatives, and holding times
with your analytical laboratory before each sampling event, as
requirements vary by method.
:::


## 9. Quality Control

### 9.1 Field Blanks

At least one field blank per sampling event: fill a sample bottle with
deionized water at the field site, preserve and handle identically to
field samples, and submit to the laboratory.

### 9.2 Field Duplicates

Collect one field duplicate per 10 samples (or at least one per
event). Duplicates are collected at the same time and location as the
primary sample.

### 9.3 Equipment Blanks

If non-dedicated sampling equipment is used (e.g., shared extension
poles, buckets), rinse the equipment with deionized water and collect
the rinse as an equipment blank.

### 9.4 Documentation

- Complete the chain of custody form before samples leave the field
- Record all deviations from this SOP in the field notebook
- Photograph site conditions at each sampling location


## 10. Data Management

1. Enter field data (times, conditions, flow estimates, sample IDs)
   into the project database within 48 hours
2. When laboratory results are received, merge with field data and
   apply QC flags per
   [SOP-L802 Quality Control](../lab_sops/SOP-L802-quality-control.qmd)
3. Archive original field data sheets (scan if paper)
4. Version-control all analysis scripts per
   [SOP-L801 RStudio and GitHub](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd)

## 12. Training Record

Before collecting stormwater samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd),
   and [SOP-F400 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F400-surface-water-sampling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the safety rules in Section 4.2 with the field lead
3. Participate in at least one supervised storm sampling event,
   including mobilization, sample collection, preservation, and COC
   completion
4. Demonstrate proper grab and composite sampling techniques
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
